approach_variants.name: Henrys Fork Trail to Anderson Pass
approach_variants.notes:
Kings Peak is reached from the Wyoming side. From Mountain View, Wyoming, head south on WY-410 toward Robertson. After roughly 6.5 to 7 miles, leave the highway where it bends hard right and continue on the graded dirt county road for about 12 miles to a signed fork for Henrys Fork. Turn onto that road and follow it roughly 10 to 12 miles to the Henrys Fork campground and trailhead, at about 9,400 ft, which has a pit toilet and no water. The road is ordinary dirt that a passenger car can manage, but it is long, so budget about an hour from town.

Walk south on the main Henrys Fork Trail up the basin. You pass an unsigned side path to Alligator Lake on the right, then cross the creek at Elkhorn Crossing, roughly 5.25 to 5.5 miles from the car. Keep to the main trail up the valley to Dollar Lake, about 8 miles in, the usual first-night camp. From the lake the trail climbs steeply to Gunsight Pass. Past the pass you can either drop into Painter Basin on the maintained trail, or take the upper shortcut that leaves to the right at the top of the pass and contours southwest above the rocks, rejoining the route below Anderson Pass. Expect about 13 to 16 miles one way depending on the line, and a net climb of roughly 4,100 to 4,250 ft to the summit.

If you go by way of Painter Basin, turn right (west) at the south side of the basin and climb to Anderson Pass. The pass is where this route's climbing begins: from it, work south up the ridge and slopes to the summit, about a mile and just under 1,000 ft above. Snow, when present, only lasts into early summer, and without it the pitch is a steep walk.
hazards: Very long approach: most parties camp near Dollar Lake
Unsigned junctions: Alligator Lake spur and the Painter Basin cutoff are easy to miss
Snow may linger on the upper slopes into early summer
approach_variants.baseFinding: You are at the start of the climb when you stand on Anderson Pass, reached either from the south side of Painter Basin or by the upper shortcut, with the broad ridge of Kings Peak rising south of you.

review.facts: Trailhead position about 40.91N 110.33W: roadtripryan (40d54m34s, 110d19m52s) + Forest Service page (40.9096, -110.3304) + stavislost (40.9096, -110.3306). Drive from Mountain View WY on WY-410 about 6.4-7 mi then dirt road ~12 mi: roadtripryan + thepeakseeker; final stretch 10.4 mi (roadtripryan) vs about 12 mi (thepeakseeker), so given as 10-12; the signed fork turn is described as left (roadtripryan) vs east (thepeakseeker). Any car can do the road: stavislost + roadtripryan (good graded dirt). Elkhorn Crossing about 5.25 mi (roadtripryan) and first junction about 5.5 mi (thepeakseeker). Dollar Lake about 8 mi: roadtripryan only (also appears in search results but not a fetched page), so the number is given as 'about 8' with moderate weight. One-way distance: 13 mi (stavislost, 26.1 mi out and back via shortcut) to 16.5 mi (thepeakseeker, 33 mi out and back); roadtripryan implies about 13-15. Net gain: 4,084 ft (roadtripryan, 13,527 minus 9,443) vs 4,250 ft (thepeakseeker). Gunsight Pass then Painter Basin then Anderson Pass: roadtripryan + thepeakseeker. Shortcut rejoining below Anderson Pass: roadtripryan + stavislost. Summit just under 1,000 ft above the pass: thepeakseeker; roadtripryan says scramble south along the ridge. Omitted because only one fetched page: parking fee (Forest Service page lists a day-use fee and honors federal passes; roadtripryan and others silent) and road closure season (not on any fetched page). The snow couloir in the stored overview was not confirmed by any fetched page.

approach_variants.name: Broads Fork Trail
approach_variants.notes:
Drive to Big Cottonwood Canyon from Salt Lake City: take I-215 to exit 6, go east on 6200 South (it becomes Wasatch Boulevard) and turn toward Big Cottonwood Canyon at the stoplight. The trailhead is about 4.5 miles up the canyon road (UT-190), on the south side at the bottom of the S-curve. The Mill B lot is shared with the Lake Blanche trail, and the Broads Fork path begins at the southwest corner. A small overflow area sits just up the road. No fee or permit is needed to park for this hike.

The path climbs steadily west, enters the Twin Peaks Wilderness early on, and crosses a footbridge beside a cascade roughly a mile in. Further up it reaches the lower meadow and beaver ponds, about 2.3 miles and 2,000 ft above the car. Beyond the ponds the trail fades into a streambed, and you must find your own line. Count on about 4.3 to 4.5 miles one way to the summit and 5,100 to 5,350 ft of gain; the day is long and steep.

From the ponds, climb the terraced slope to the upper meadow near 9,600 ft, then scramble up rock toward the saddle on the ridge, around 10,800 ft. Snow can sit in the cirque into summer. From the saddle, follow the ridge to the East Twin summit. A well-used variation leaves the trail at the meadow and heads up the open gully to the right (Robinson's Variation); it is very steep, mostly hands-and-feet over boulders.
hazards: Trail disappears above the beaver ponds: route-finding required
Lingering snow in the cirque and on the saddle into summer
Steep boulders and loose rock in the gully; exposed third-class scramble near the top
Long day with a big total climb; start early
approach_variants.baseFinding: The trail ends at the beaver ponds in the broad glacial meadow below the Twin Peaks cirque; from there the walking route turns into off-trail streambed, terraces and boulders toward the ridge.

review.facts: Trailhead at the S-curve on the right (south) side, mile 4.7 (roadtripryan) vs about 4.5 (utahoutdooractivities) vs 4.2 (visitutah, for the adjoining Mill B South lot); given as about 4.5. Shared lot with Lake Blanche trail: girlonahike + roadtripryan (Lake Blanche trail starts on east side of the same lot). Directions I-215 exit 6, 6200 South to Wasatch Blvd, turn toward Big Cottonwood Canyon: roadtripryan + utahoutdooractivities + visitutah (the last two disagree on the exact cross street used). Trail starts at southwest corner of lot: girlonahike + utahoutdooractivities (west corner). Distance one way: about 4.5 mi, some say 5.0 (utahoutdooractivities) vs 8.52 mi out and back, about 4.26 one way (onxmaps); given as 4.3-4.5. Gain: 5,130 ft (utahoutdooractivities) vs 5,345 ft (onxmaps); girlonahike lists 5,960 ft for a loop with the variation. Bridge near a cascade about 1 mi: onxmaps + girlonahike (roadtripryan 1.2 mi). Meadow with beaver ponds: onxmaps + girlonahike + utahoutdooractivities. Pond about 2.3 mi and 2,040 ft up: utahoutdooractivities (single, given as approximate). Trail fades beyond: utahoutdooractivities + onxmaps. Saddle near 10,800 ft: utahoutdooractivities (single); upper meadow 9,600: single. Robinson's Variation leaves at the meadow: girlonahike (also seen in search results). No fee or permit: girlonahike (none) + visitutah (no fees at the Mill B South lot). Wilderness boundary: utahoutdooractivities + visitutah. No seasonal road closure found on any fetched page, so none stated.
